# Issues

**Summary:** 11 candidates considered · 7 raised · 4 refuted. By severity: High 1, Medium 5, Low 1. By family: IF-4 (documentation/design drift) 6, IF-3a (implicit coupling) 1. DeepInit is report-only, so nothing here was changed in source, and only findings with HIGH certainty are raised. IF-2 (database drift) does not apply because there is no database. IF-5 (git risk) is unavailable because the repository has no commits.

All references below were re-checked against the source after the live-combat change landed on 2026-10-21. Lifecycles and resolutions were updated by hand on 2026-10-27, after the design-audit fixes; the next DeepInit run regenerates this file.

## Fires (raised)

### ISS-001 — IF-4 — The design says discoveries pause activity; the code never does
- **family:** IF-4
- **claim:** Possible design/code drift. The implementation plan, ADR 0007 and the README say away time advances an activity only to its objective or the next meaningful discovery, and that a discovery can pause it. The engine logs discoveries without pausing. The validator rejects `pause` on events ("discoveries never stop activity") and lists `pauseOnReveal` as a removed field, and a test pins the non-pausing behaviour. No ADR records the removal, so anyone who "fixes" the engine to match the docs would break tested behaviour.
- **provenance:** `design/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:25`, `design/decisions/0007-away-time-and-acceleration.md:7`, `design/decisions/0025-lifespan-and-checkpoints-cut.md:21`, `README.md:35`, `src/engine.ts:1243-1261`, `scripts/validate.ts:37`, `scripts/validate.ts:169`, `tests/engine.test.ts:284`
- **severity:** Medium
- **criticality:** Core
- **certainty:** HIGH
- **lifecycle:** resolved (2026-10-27)
- **resolution:** [ADR 0027](../../design/decisions/0027-locks-at-payment-and-stops.md) records that discoveries never stop activity and amends ADR 0007's stops. The implementation plan's away-time paragraph and the README now say an activity stops at its objective, a full store or an unaffordable drain, then the waiting list and Rest run, and only the rest is banked.
- **baseline:** new
- **suggested direction:** Record the decision in an ADR and update the plan and README, or restore pausing deliberately.

### ISS-002 — IF-4 — The report designated as the one current pacing figure is stale
- **family:** IF-4
- **claim:** Possible stale source of truth. The design plan names `playtest/SIMULATION-REPORT.md` as the one current Foundation figure. That report states 28.63/28.08 min against a 25–35 min window, with 113/113 records. `bun run validate` on this run measured 13.00 min (channel-only) and 14.90 min (hollow-only) against a 12–20 min target, with 109/109 records. Anyone trusting the designated source gets roughly twice the real pacing.
- **provenance:** `design/DESIGN-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:11`, `playtest/SIMULATION-REPORT.md:7`, `scripts/validate.ts:29-30`, `scripts/validate.ts:293-294`
- **severity:** Medium
- **criticality:** Supporting
- **certainty:** HIGH
- **lifecycle:** resolved (2026-10-27)
- **resolution:** The report's current-pacing paragraph now carries the 27 October `bun run validate` figures and bands (direct routes 9.47 / 10.73 min to Foundation, 119/119 records) and marks the older sections as history; [ADR 0028](../../design/decisions/0028-ten-minute-foundation.md) names it as where the measured figure lives.
- **baseline:** new
- **suggested direction:** Regenerate the report from `bun run validate --json`.

### ISS-003 — IF-4 — Three different pacing bounds
- **family:** IF-4
- **claim:** Possible conflicting rules. Design plan Part E item 4 and §C call for sustained-tempo Foundation within 45 min, with the clicked time reported beside it, and Circulation open by 27 min. The validator enforces 720–1200 s (12–20 min) and an 850 s Circulation window on the direct routes, and measures no sustained-only route. `scripts/routes.ts` exits non-zero above 2700 s (45 min). The README's "about fifteen active minutes" agrees only with the validator, and the sustained-only figure the design asks for is never produced.
- **provenance:** `design/DESIGN-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:179`, `design/DESIGN-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:372`, `scripts/validate.ts:28-32`, `scripts/validate.ts:238-252`, `scripts/routes.ts:445`, `README.md:37`
- **severity:** Medium
- **criticality:** Supporting
- **certainty:** HIGH
- **lifecycle:** resolved (2026-10-27)
- **resolution:** One bound, recorded in [ADR 0028](../../design/decisions/0028-ten-minute-foundation.md): about ten minutes of honest play, enforced only by `bun run validate` (direct routes 480–780 s with Circulation by 600 s; preference routes within 1200 s; ridge 720–1440 s). The design plan's Part C bound and Part E check 4, the README and PRODUCT.md now say the same; `scripts/routes.ts` no longer exits on a time of its own; and with the sustained earners gone (ADR 0022 amendment) there is no sustained-only figure to report.
- **baseline:** new
- **suggested direction:** Pick one bound, record it, and align `routes.ts` and the plan.

### ISS-004 — IF-4 — The route-key rules from ADR 0024 are not in force
- **family:** IF-4
- **claim:** Possible unenforced design rule. ADR 0024, the design plan and the implementation plan say three things: the shared module holds `t_` key records shown under Methods; no gate names another module's record id; and the validator runs three key checks. The code differs on each. No `t_` records exist, so keys are only tag counters, and the validator rejects a record whose id equals a tag, so a key record cannot be added as written. Tooltips show the raw tag strings. Ridge and shared gates name opening ids (`cot`, `garden_plot`, `strongbox`, `lean_to`, `jade_slip`). The validator has no carried/read checks, and `t_school_body` and `t_school_earth` are carried but never read. As a result, renaming an opening record silently changes ridge gates.
- **provenance:** `design/decisions/0024-route-keys.md:13`, `design/decisions/0024-route-keys.md:32`, `design/DESIGN-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:359`, `design/DESIGN-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:375`, `design/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:11`, `README.md:39`, `src/engine.ts:177-180`, `src/engine.ts:1372`, `scripts/validate.ts:120`, `src/data/ridge.json:141`, `src/data/ridge.json:301`, `src/data/ridge.json:307`, `src/data/shared.json:26`, `src/data/opening.json:125`, `src/data/opening.json:136`
- **severity:** Medium
- **criticality:** Core
- **certainty:** HIGH
- **lifecycle:** resolved (2026-10-27)
- **resolution:** ADR 0024 is amended to match the code: keys are named in `routeKeys` (`src/content.ts`) rather than as records, and show by name on Character and in method details. The ridge reads every school key (its four direction signs), adds the sword and formation keys, and `bun run validate` fails a key carried but never read, a carried key without a name and a named key nothing carries. Commit 94a21fe closed the rest: the direction signs read a new `t_furnished` key carried by the cot, herb plot and strongbox instead of naming them; the coffer asks only `g.foundation > 0` and the cottage `g.foundation > 0 && g.home_space.max >= 4`; and `validateModuleSeams` (`scripts/validate.ts:282`) fails any gate in `opening.json` or `ridge.json` that names a record from the other chapter. The shared file is exempt as the vocabulary both chapters read.
- **baseline:** new
- **suggested direction:** Either implement the checks and key records, or amend ADR 0024 to match the code.

### ISS-005 — IF-4 — A save is refused when content retires a technique, activity or fight id
- **family:** IF-4
- **claim:** Possible contradiction of a documented invariant. `decodeSave` documents that "ids the content no longer has are skipped rather than refused", but that holds only for `items`. The other fields fail on an unknown id: `attuned` is validated against known ids; the running and waiting entries go through `readTask`/`readObjective`; and a saved fight must still name a record with an encounter (`readFight`). When decoding fails, both IndexedDB slots fail, boot falls through to the "needs attention" screen, and an exported file of the same journey is refused too. The test for departed ids covers `items` only.
- **provenance:** `src/persistence.ts:147-150`, `src/persistence.ts:67-68`, `src/persistence.ts:113`, `src/persistence.ts:129`, `src/persistence.ts:138-141`, `src/persistence.ts:199`, `src/persistence.ts:219-223`, `src/persistence.ts:291-296`, `src/main.ts:44-71`, `tests/persistence.test.ts:70-80`
- **severity:** High
- **criticality:** Core
- **certainty:** HIGH
- **lifecycle:** open
- **baseline:** new
- **suggested direction:** Filter unknown ids out of `attuned`, `active`, `waiting` and `fight` (dropping the entry), and add tests.

### ISS-006 — IF-3a — The UI hardcodes content ids that the validator never checks
- **family:** IF-3a
- **claim:** Possible silent cross-component coupling. `src/ui.ts` names `vigor`, `qi`, `life`, `strain`, `rest`, `coin`, `jade_slip`, `home_space`, `foundation` and others directly, and `engine.stat("home_space")` throws on an unknown id. The validator never sees the UI; only the browser smoke test would catch a rename. A content rename would crash rendering, and the ticker would then stop.
- **provenance:** `src/ui.ts:45`, `src/ui.ts:595`, `src/ui.ts:650`, `src/ui.ts:907`, `src/ui.ts:1011`, `src/engine.ts:154-158`, `src/main.ts:146-151`
- **severity:** Low
- **criticality:** Supporting
- **certainty:** HIGH
- **lifecycle:** open
- **baseline:** new
- **suggested direction:** Export these ids as constants beside `HOME_SPACE`/`ATTUNE_SLOTS` and have the validator require them.

### ISS-007 — IF-4 — The agent instructions and the implementation plan understate the slice's scope
- **family:** IF-4
- **claim:** Possible stale scope. `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` describe the current slice as the village to Foundation, with combat, classes and the waystation out of scope, and the implementation plan says "No … classes, waystation". The code ships the ridge chapter with a waystation, a class record and fights. ADR 0026 is accepted for chapter 1 and the ridge, and the README now says the slice has one fight before Foundation and one on the ridge. Agents may refuse or undo in-scope ridge and combat work.
- **provenance:** `AGENTS.md:89`, `CLAUDE.md:89`, `design/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-2026-10-18.md:3`, `src/data/ridge.json:236`, `src/data/opening.json:63`, `src/data/opening.json:235`, `design/decisions/0026-combat-exchanges.md:3`, `README.md:58`
- **severity:** Medium
- **criticality:** Supporting
- **certainty:** HIGH
- **lifecycle:** resolved (2026-10-27)
- **resolution:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and the implementation plan's scope line now name the ridge chapter, its four direction classes, the waystation and the two optional fights as in scope; sects, waystation modules and dungeons stay out.
- **baseline:** new
- **suggested direction:** A human should update the scope line; DeepInit carried it forward verbatim.

## Refuted candidates (not raised)
| Candidate | Why refuted |
|---|---|
| 11 unsourced cap lines on coverage and ridge routes | All are end-of-slice caps. Rule 11 applies only "if visible", and the validator deliberately scopes it to opening routes (`scripts/validate.ts:256`) |
| Empty `catch` in `SaveStore.write` | Deliberate: keeps a valid backup when current storage is damaged (`src/persistence.ts:309`) |
| Empty `catch` around localStorage | Preferences only (`src/ui.ts:471`) |
| The stall guard clears the slot without a journal line | Deliberate per its comment: content that starts but can never tick must not spin. Only broken content reaches it, and every validated route completes (`src/engine.ts:692-695`) |
